clue.text: Hard to crack shell, with nut

indicators.note: the letter for hard breaks into the shell word, splitting it open

parts.note: a shell is a case or casing
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A tough nut whose shell is hard to crack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to crack' puts H inside CASE, and W follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The kidney-shaped cashew is a familiar edible nut, sold roasted and salted.

clue.text: Is blocking appeal a quality that's appealing?

indicators.note: blocking means sitting in the way, so the word is put inside

parts.note: charm is appeal or attractiveness
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether some attractive trait is getting in the way of a legal appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'appeal' is attractiveness, but the definition's question mark marks a cheeky echo: the answer is itself an appealing quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is a compelling personal magnetism that draws others in.

clue.text: Bit of glass with point, unyielding

parts.note: S, south, is a compass point
something unyielding is hard

explanation.surface: A tough sliver of glass with a sharp tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A shard is a sharp broken fragment, often of glass or pottery.

clue.text: Time starts to elapse rather alarmingly

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Time is slipping away at a worrying pace.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a long period of time in history.

clue.text: Three cast as insignificant

parts.note: TRI is the prefix meaning three, as in tricycle
to cast is to fling or throw

explanation.surface: Three actors cast in such minor parts that they hardly matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trivial and of little importance is insignificant.

clue.text: Dish with fine taste

parts.note: rare means fine or excellent, as in a rare old time
a bit is a taste, a small amount

explanation.surface: A meal served with a delicate flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is cheese melted on toast, a British supper dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit, cheese melted on toast, is a savoury dish.

clue.text: Claim to catch grandma in a state, as outcast

indicators.note: in places everything else inside the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: FL is the abbreviation for Florida, a US state

indicators.note: catch means hold inside, so the word for grandma goes into the claim

parts.note: to allege is to claim
nan is an informal word for grandmother

explanation.surface: Someone says they caught their grandmother in a terrible state, cast out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to catch' puts NAN inside ALLEGE, and 'in' puts that inside FL, the abbreviation for Florida. 'a state' looks like a mood, but it is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: A fallen angel is Lucifer or another angel cast out of heaven, the very picture of an outcast.

clue.text: Because of that very cheap furniture item, tons going into business

parts.note: a sofa costing 1P, one penny, written as I P SOFA

indicators.note: going into means the tons letter is put inside the business word

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: A bargain-basement sofa, sold by the ton, explains a company's business model.
explanation.walkthrough: The digit 1 is read as the letter I, so a one-penny (1P) sofa gives IPSOFA. 'very' looks like part of the definition but belongs to 'very cheap'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin tag means by that very fact, so it explains a consequence as following from that.

clue.text: Opener around a long time, offered spin

indicators.note: around means the opener's letters go round the time word

parts.note: a gate is something that opens
YR, year, is a long stretch of time

explanation.surface: Someone opening the batting has been in for ages and offered some spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offered' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To gyrate is to spin or whirl round in a circle.

clue.text: Still work widely accepted in government

indicators.note: in places the letter for widely accepted inside the government word

parts.note: the state is the government
U, universal, is the film rating for viewing by everyone, so widely accepted

explanation.surface: A piece of work that is still widely accepted within government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still work' looks like 'still working', but it is a work of art that does not move.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted figure, a work of art that stands motionless.

clue.text: White substance provided, as one preparing joint?

parts.note: A LA, from the French, means in the manner of, so as
a baster spoons fat over a roasting joint of meat as it cooks

explanation.surface: A white powder supplied, as if by a cook getting the Sunday roast ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided' just links the definition to the wordplay. A joint here is a cut of meat for roasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a fine white mineral, a form of gypsum, carved into ornaments.

clue.text: Flop, regarding sun, heading west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left, so the pieces run backwards

parts.note: RE means regarding, on the subject of
SOL is the Latin for the sun

explanation.surface: A failure on the subject of the sun as it sets in the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading west' turns RESOL around.
explanation.definitionFit: A flop is a failure, and someone who fails is a loser.

clue.text: Ruthless ambition led astray

indicators.note: astray means wandering off course, so these letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone's pitiless ambition led them down the wrong path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' is the anagram signal; 'led' belongs to the fodder, though the surface reads it as 'led astray'. Indomitable fits 'ruthless' only loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: someone unstoppable and unrelenting can be called ruthless in pursuing a goal.

clue.text: Artist outlining second capital city, a fine thing to hang

indicators.note: outlining means drawing round, so the artist goes round the rest

parts.note: Claude Monet was the French Impressionist painter
Quito is the capital of Ecuador

explanation.surface: An artist depicts a capital city in a fine picture to hang on the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine thing to hang' suggests a painting by the artist, but it is a fine mesh hung over a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosquito net is a fine mesh hung over a bed to keep insects off.

clue.text: Well, attack!

definitions.meaning: in good health, healthy and in shape
a sudden bout, such as of coughing or rage

explanation.definitionFit: Being healthy is being in shape, and a sudden seizure or outburst is also a fit.

clue.text: Wonderful picture an inspiration, inspiring reviewing set

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the muse takes the other letters inside

parts.note: a muse is a source of artistic inspiration

indicators.note: re-viewing means looking at again in a new way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A great film inspires its viewers, and a film set keeps being reviewed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewing' looks like film criticism, fitting 'picture', but it signals rearranging. The definition is by example: a wonderful film is one thing called must-see.
explanation.definitionFit: A film so good it should not be missed is called a must-see by critics.

clue.text: Lower, held high?

parts.note: a lower is something that moos, a cow, and one held in high regard is one never to be criticized

explanation.definitionFit: An idea or institution treated as beyond criticism, after the cows Hindus venerate.

clue.text: Country requiring new leader, in state of shock

indicators.note: the first letter of the country is swapped for a different one

parts.note: France is the European country

explanation.surface: A nation that needs a fresh head of state, left in a stunned condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requiring new leader' replaces the F of FRANCE with T; the clue leaves the solver to find which letter fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A trance is a dazed, stunned condition like hypnosis or shock.

clue.text: What's in dad's scabbard? Keep it secret

parts.note: PA'S, belonging to dad
what's in a scabbard is a sword

explanation.surface: A father hides something in his sword sheath and asks for silence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's in' points from the scabbard to the blade it holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A password is a secret word one must keep to oneself.

clue.text: Tramp showing bit of neck?

definitions.meaning: the back of the neck, by which a kitten is lifted

explanation.definitionFit: A scruffy person is informally called this, and the nape of the neck is also called the scruff.

clue.text: Hopeful ploy at cards brings expression of dismay, holding head

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the dismay word goes round the head word

parts.note: fie is an old exclamation of dismay or disgust
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Dungeness

explanation.surface: A card player's speculative trick draws a groan from the player in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, a finesse is a play that hopes a particular card lies with a particular opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge or whist, a finesse is a speculative play hoping a key card is favourably placed.

clue.text: Young lady in sarong I survey from behind

indicators.note: from behind says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Looking at a young woman in a sarong from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the hidden run ARONGIS, which 'from behind' turns around.
explanation.definitionFit: Signora is the Italian title for a married woman, used here loosely for a lady.

clue.text: Revealing what's up, naughty boy boxed

indicators.note: boxed means enclosed, so the sky goes round the naughty boy

parts.note: the sky is what is up above
an imp is a mischievous child

explanation.surface: A naughty boy gets boxed for showing off what's going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what's up' sounds like 'what's happening', but it means the sky overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimpy clothing is scanty and shows plenty of skin, so it is revealing.

clue.text: Distant Piscean?

definitions.meaning: read as ..., as Pisces is the fish sign of the zodiac

explanation.definitionFit: Being aloof and unfriendly is being standoffish; split, the word also reads 'of fish'.

clue.text: Hot drink, half price

indicators.note: only half of the drink's six letters is kept, the back three

parts.note: coffee is a hot drink

explanation.surface: A hot drink sold at half price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' drops COF, the first three letters of COFFEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fee is a charge or price paid for a service.

clue.text: Evidence of epidemic, I can confirm, disease

parts.note: an epidemic shows itself as TONS ILL, very many people sick
IT IS is what someone says to confirm something

explanation.surface: A doctor confirms the signs of an epidemic of illness.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer's letters as a phrase: tons ill, it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the tonsils is a common infection, so a disease.

clue.text: Present comforting word

definitions.meaning: said repeatedly to soothe someone upset, as in 'never mind, dear'

explanation.definitionFit: Being in attendance means being on the spot, and the soothing phrase repeats the same adverb twice.

clue.text: Ultimately, film is describing ancient civilization

definitions.meaning: a finished film is said to be in the can
an adjective used of the old empire of Peru

explanation.surface: In the end a movie gets made, telling of a lost civilization.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for the Andean empire that the Spanish conquered in Peru.

clue.text: Computer's back up here so corrupted in big screen saver?

indicators.note: in places the final letter of the computer word inside the shuffled letters
corrupted data is scrambled, so these letters are rearranged
the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A computer screensaver glitches and gets scrambled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupted' rearranges UPHERESO to SUPEHERO, and 'in' puts R, the 'back' of computer, inside. A big screen is cinema, so its saver is a film hero.
explanation.definitionFit: A caped crusader who rescues people in blockbuster films is a saver on the cinema screen.

clue.text: Port or whiskey

definitions.meaning: a harbour town in East Sussex, one of England's old Cinque Ports
a whiskey distilled mainly from this grain, popular in North America

explanation.definitionFit: The Sussex town is one of the historic Cinque Ports, and the grain gives its name to a North American whiskey.

clue.text: One's fired a question: it's come to nothing, briefly

parts.note: how is a question word
the word it, with the possessive dropped

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the word for nothing goes

parts.note: zero means nothing

explanation.surface: Someone sacked asks how it all came to nothing so quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' clips ZERO to ZER. 'One's fired' looks like a sacking, but it is a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A howitzer is a short-barrelled artillery gun, something fired at the enemy.

clue.text: One always remembered on purpose

parts.note: in cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side
an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: Someone deliberately makes themselves unforgettable.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side, also called leg, is the half of the field behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a famous person whose name lives on in memory.
